slides.title: Five ratios every business student should *read at a glance*
slides.sub: The formula, a worked example and what each one tells you.

slides.label: Ratio 01 of 05
slides.title: Gross margin
slides.tells: How much of every sales dollar is left after paying for what was sold.

slides.label: Ratio 02 of 05
slides.title: Current ratio
slides.tells: Whether the business can cover the bills due within a year.

slides.label: Ratio 03 of 05
slides.title: Return on equity
slides.tells: How much profit the business earns on each dollar its owners have put in.

slides.label: Ratio 04 of 05
slides.title: Break-even point
slides.formula: Fixed costs|÷ (Price − Variable cost per unit)
slides.tells: How many units must be sold before the business stops making a loss.

slides.label: Ratio 05 of 05
slides.title: Debt to equity
slides.tells: How heavily the business leans on borrowing compared with owners' money.

slides.note: Save this one for exam week.

slides.label: The working

slides.question: Fixed costs are $84,000. Each unit sells for $40 and costs $26 to make. How many units to break even?
lines: Contribution per unit = $40 − $26 = $14
Break-even = $84,000 ÷ $40
Break-even = 2,100 units

slides.label: The answer
slides.title: Line 2 divides by the *wrong number*.
slides.question: Break-even divides fixed costs by the contribution per unit, not by the selling price.
lines: Contribution per unit = $40 − $26 = $14
Break-even = $84,000 ÷ $40
Break-even = 2,100 units

slides.title: Four small slips that cost marks in *accounting and finance*
slides.sub: None of them is about not knowing the content.

slides.label: Slip 01 of 04
slides.title: Mixing up margin and markup
slides.body: Margin divides profit by revenue. Markup divides profit by cost. Same profit, two very different answers.

slides.label: Slip 02 of 04
slides.title: Rounding too early
slides.body: Round a growth factor in the middle of a question and the error grows with every step after it.

slides.label: Slip 03 of 04
slides.title: Losing the minus sign in NPV
slides.body: The money you invest at the start is a cash outflow, so it goes in as a negative.

slides.label: Slip 04 of 04
slides.title: Annual rate, monthly periods
slides.body: If interest compounds monthly, both the rate and the number of periods have to be monthly.
slides.wrong: 12% a year for 3 years, monthly:|i = 12%, n = 3

slides.label: The pattern
slides.title: You knew the method every time. The slip was in *one line*.
body: That is the kind of mistake StudyCrest is built for. It checks every line of your working while you write and flags the one that went wrong.
